validity.researcher_notes: The pipeline physically and legally exists and is correctly classified as an operating gas transmission lateral -- existence is NOT in doubt (see below). The one real defect is attribution: the row's recorded PipelineName is 'Columbia Gas Transmission' and its Owner1 is 'Columbia Gas Transmission LLC', but every independent primary source names the applicant/owner/operator as 'Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC' (a separate TC Energy subsidiary from Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC -- both exist as distinct FERC-jurisdictional pipelines under the TC Energy/TransCanada umbrella). Checked: (1) FERC Federal Register Notice of Application, Docket CP20-527-000, 10/15/2020: 'Take notice that on September 24, 2020, Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC (Columbia Gulf) ... filed an application ... requesting authorization of its East Lateral XPress Project.' (2) TC Energy's own project fact sheet: 'firm natural gas transportation service on TC Energy's Columbia Gulf Transmission (CGT) East Lateral Pipeline system.' (3) NOAA Fisheries incidental-take page, title 'TC Energy Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC's East Lateral XPRESS Project', notice 04/10/2024: 'NOAA Fisheries has issued an incidental harassment authorization to Columbia Gulf, LLC.' (4) Gas Compression Magazine (Wayback capture, 2021-04-26): 'Columbia Gulf Transmission LLC (Columbia Gulf) has received a favorable environmental assessment from FERC for its East Lateral Xpress project.' (5) TC Energy's own 2022 10-K MD&A (SEC EDGAR, trp-12312022xmda.htm): lists it under 'Major projects under construction' as 'East Lateral XPress ... An expansion project on Columbia Gulf through compressor station modifications and additions.' Four independent origins (FERC/federal regulator, the operator's own fact sheet and SEC filing, a federal wildlife-authorization notice, and trade press) unanimously name Columbia Gulf, none name Columbia Gas. This matches the batch scope note ('LXP is a Columbia GULF expansion in practice ... the row's PipelineName may be wrong') and the roster: P6533 'Columbia Gulf Transmission Pipeline' is the separate system row this project belongs under. Recommend re-attributing PipelineName/Owner1/Operator to Columbia Gulf Transmission, LLC and treating P3188 as a Columbia Gulf project row rather than a Columbia Gas one (not a duplicate of any roster row -- P2556 Louisiana XPress and P4448 Mainline 100/200 Replacement are separate, distinct Columbia projects, and P6533 is the system-level row, not a project-level duplicate).

validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: overwhelming, multi-origin confirmation -- FERC docket CP20-527 (Notice of Application 2020-10-15, Notice of Schedule for EA 2020-12-07, Notice of Intent for EIS 2021-06-03), NOAA Fisheries incidental-take authorization for pile-driving construction (2024-04-10), TC Energy's own project fact sheet and 2022/2023 10-K/earnings disclosures, EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects tracker (28 releases, 2021-01 through 2026-08, docket-matched), and Gas Compression Magazine trade coverage. This is not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as an operating interstate gas transmission lateral/expansion (NGA section 7(c) certificated); not a gathering or gas-processing line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 41-row roster and the batch's Columbia-family note -- not a duplicate of P2556 (Louisiana XPress, a separate Columbia project), P4448 (Mainline 100/200 Replacement, Kentucky), or P6533 (the Columbia Gulf system-level row, which is a network aggregate, not a project). Plaquemines-area rows P2536 (Evangeline Pass) and P3193/P5415 (Gator Express) are interconnecting deliveries to/from ELXP's new meter station, not the same physical pipe. SPEC (Capacity, the EIA-flagged 'differs'): the sheet's 183.00 MMcf/d is CORRECT as recorded -- it is the project's own NEW/incremental capacity, not the combined system total. TC Energy's fact sheet states verbatim: 'ELXP will create 183 MDth/d of incremental capacity. This incremental capacity, along with the utilization of existing capacity on CGT's system, will allow for the full project capacity ... of 725 MDth/d' (575 MDth/d from CGT's existing Rayne pool + 150 MDth/d from an existing Venice meter station). The FERC Notice of Application independently states the same figure: 'The Project will create 183,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of incremental [capacity].' EIA's own release history confirms this: every release from 2021-01 through 2025-10 (18 consecutive releases) reported Capacity=183 MMcf/d for this project; only the two most recent releases (2026-05, 2026-08) changed the figure to 725, evidently a late correction/re-scoping in EIA's own workbook to the aggregate delivered total rather than the incremental figure the project actually added. Per the aggregate-vs-segment rule, 725 is a SYSTEM/combined figure and is not a valid replacement for this project's own 183 MMcf/d incremental capacity -- the sheet is right and EIA's newest releases are the outlier. No spec concern filed; see fills[] for the Capacity REFS_ADDED record and the researcher_notes there for the full release-history evidence.

Investigated whether Delayed=yes is actually correct. Every dated source found gives a CONSISTENT schedule with no sign of slippage: TC Energy's fact sheet (2023) states 'Project construction anticipated in 2024 with 2025 in-service delivery' -- and the project was in fact completed on that exact schedule (EIA: Construction status by 2024-01 release, Completed by 2025-07 release, in-service May 2025). The FERC EIS process did take the longer environmental-impact-statement track (NOI 2021-06-03, Draft EIS 2021-06-03, Final EIS 2021-07-01) rather than a faster EA-only review, which lengthens the PRE-construction timeline relative to a simple EA, but I found no source stating the project's own anticipated in-service date was ever pushed back from an earlier target, nor any FERC order, operator statement, or press report using the word 'delay' for this specific project. This raises a real possibility that Delayed=yes/DelayType=inferred is itself a sheet error (perhaps inferred from the multi-year FERC review process rather than an actual schedule slip), but I could not find a dated source that either confirms a specific slipped milestone (to support the value) or explicitly states there was no delay (to support removing it), so I am not proposing a correction -- flagging it here for a human researcher rather than silently either keeping or removing an inferred flag with no ref either way. The EIA pre-matched candidate block flags Capacity as 'differs' (sheet 183.0 vs EIA-Aug2026 725.0) -- investigated per the aggregate-vs-segment rule. Resolution: 183 is CORRECT for this project. TC Energy's own fact sheet and FERC's own Federal Register notice (the applicant's own filing) both state, in nearly identical language, that ELXP itself creates 183,000 Dth/d of NEW/incremental capacity, and that this combines with EXISTING capacity elsewhere on Columbia Gulf's system (575 MDth/d from an existing pool + 150 MDth/d from an existing meter station) to reach a combined delivered total of 725 MDth/d. 725 is therefore a system-wide aggregate, not this segment's own capacity, and is not a valid ref for this cell (aggregate-vs-segment rule). This is independently confirmed by EIA's own release-history: sources/eia_pipeline_projects/data/eia_projects_long.csv shows Capacity=183 reported consistently across every release from 2021-01 through 2025-10 (18 releases) for this docket; only the two most recent releases (2026-05, 2026-08) revised the figure to 725, which reads as a late change in what EIA is measuring (project addition vs. combined delivered total) rather than a correction of a prior error. Filed as a validity 'confirmed (caveat)' entry (no spec concern) rather than a correction, since sheet, FERC, and TC Energy's own numbers all agree the segment adds 183 MMcf/d.

Searched the FERC application notice and the three subsequent Federal Register notices in docket CP20-527 (Schedule for EA, NOI for EIS text), TC Energy's fact sheet, NOAA Fisheries' final IHA notice and its linked application/monitoring-report titles, Gas Compression Magazine, and the route geojson properties -- none state a MAOP or operating-pressure figure for this specific lateral. FERC certificate orders and EAs/EISs for laterals of this size sometimes omit a stated MAOP in the notice text itself (it appears in engineering exhibits not indexed by Federal Register/regulations.gov search), and PHMSA's public-facing pipeline datasets report MAOP at the operator/system level, not per-project. Did not find a PHMSA special-permit or annual-report figure specific to the new EL-300 lateral (only found unrelated MAOP figures for other, older CGT mainline segments, which would be an aggregate-vs-segment mismatch if applied here). Leaving blank rather than forcing a system-level or unrelated-segment figure onto this cell.
